Latin word

tamquam

tamquam (tamquam sī)

conjunction, with the subjunctive; without a verb, “like” · Wiktionary

as if; like; like, just as; as if

In this lexicon

  • as if

    also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 5.42: parvī enim prīmō ortū sīc jacent, tamquam omnīnō sine animō sint; Cic. Att. 8.14.2: ego tēcum tamquam mēcum loquor

  • like

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 8.14.2: ego tēcum tamquam mēcum loquor; Quint. 6.3.59: tamquam assem elephantō dēs

Examples

  • parvī enim prīmō ortū sīc jacent, tamquam omnīnō sine animō sint

    for at first, just born, little ones lie as if they had no mind at allCic. Fin. 5.42

    In the entry for as if

  • ego tēcum tamquam mēcum loquor

    I talk to you as I talk to myselfCic. Att. 8.14.2

    In the entry for as if

  • ego tēcum tamquam mēcum loquor

    I talk to you as I talk to myselfCic. Att. 8.14.2

    In the entry for like

  • tum sēmen seritō crēbrum tamquam līnum, eō terram crībrō incernitō altam digitum trānsversum

    then sow the seed thick, like flax, and sift earth over it a finger’s breadth deepCato Agr. 48.1

    In the entry for like

  • mūtāta omnia altōque cinere tamquam nive obducta

    everything was changed, and covered in deep ash, as if with snowPlin. Ep. 6.20.18

    In the entry for like

  • nōlī, inquit, tamquam assem elephantō dēs

    “Don’t hold it out,” he said, “as if you were giving a penny to an elephant”Quint. 6.3.59
